found_text: Results revealed that non-residential fathers (n = 225) were less supportive and controlling than fathers in joint custody (n = 138) and married fathers (n = 224). Nevertheless, having a supportive father was beneficial to children's self-esteem in each family structure. We conclude that, even after a divorce, fathers have the capacity to enhance children's self-esteem and we suggest that future research should investigate this capacity.
location: Abstract (sentences 7-9), Journal of Youth and Adolescence 41(12):1643-1656 (2012), doi:10.1007/s10964-012-9783-6
proposed_ar: كشفت النتائج أن الآباء غير المقيمين مع أبنائهم (225 أبا) كانوا أقل دعما ومتابعة من الآباء في الحضانة المشتركة (138 أبا) ومن الآباء المتزوجين (224 أبا). ومع ذلك كان وجود أب داعم نافعا لتقدير الأبناء لأنفسهم في كل أنواع الأسر. ونخلص إلى أن الآباء، حتى بعد الطلاق، قادرون على رفع تقدير أبنائهم لأنفسهم، ونقترح أن تبحث الدراسات المقبلة هذه القدرة.
notes: Verified on the Springer page (PubMed is bot-checked). Sample: 587 children aged 10-18 and their parents (Flanders, Belgium). The abstract ties self-esteem to the father's SUPPORT only; the gist's «ولا سيما الدعم والمتابعة» should be narrowed to support (control is reported only as lower among non-residential fathers). The second clause of the gist (involvement higher in joint custody) is supported: fathers in joint custody were more supportive and controlling than non-residential fathers.

found_text: Overall the wellbeing of children in joint physical custody is similar to that of children in other custody arrangements. However, under certain circumstances joint physical custody can become negatively related to child wellbeing. We find support for the moderating effects of parental conflict, quality of the relationship with mother and father, and the presence of a new partner in parental households.
location: Abstract (last three sentences), Journal of Family Studies 19(2):139-158 (2013), doi:10.5172/jfs.2013.19.2.139; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.5172/jfs.2013.19.2.139)
proposed_ar: على العموم كان رفاه الأطفال في الإقامة المشتركة مماثلا لرفاه الأطفال في ترتيبات الحضانة الأخرى. غير أن الإقامة المشتركة قد تصبح في ظروف معينة مرتبطة سلبا برفاه الطفل. ووجدنا ما يؤيد أثر النزاع بين الوالدين، وجودة العلاقة بالأم والأب، ووجود شريك جديد في بيت أحد الوالدين.
double_edged: However, under certain circumstances joint physical custody can become negatively related to child wellbeing. We find support for the moderating effects of parental conflict, quality of the relationship with mother and father, and the presence of a new partner in parental households.
notes: The gist's «مساويا أو أحسن» overstates: the abstract says wellbeing is SIMILAR (not better) and explicitly warns that joint physical custody can become negative under parental conflict, poor parent-child relationship, or a new partner in the household. Data: LAGO project, 1,570 children of divorced parents (Flanders). Suggest rewording to «مماثلا» and keeping the caveat, or dropping the entry. Publisher page (doi.org -> tandfonline) could not be fetched.

found_text: He shows that children growing up with two continuously married parents are less likely to experience a wide range of cognitive, emotional, and social problems, not only during childhood but also in adulthood. [...] He shows that compared with other children, those who grow up in stable, two-parent families have a higher standard of living, receive more effective parenting, experience more cooperative co-parenting, are emotionally closer to both parents, and are subjected to fewer stressful events and circumstances.
location: Summary (journal abstract), The Future of Children 15(2):75-96 (Fall 2005), doi:10.1353/foc.2005.0012; body sentence: "Interviews with children reveal that losing contact with fathers is one of the most painful outcomes of divorce."
proposed_ar: يبين [أماتو] أن الأطفال الذين ينشؤون مع والدين مستمرين في زواجهما أقل عرضة لطائفة واسعة من المشكلات الذهنية والعاطفية والاجتماعية، لا في الطفولة فحسب بل في الرشد أيضا. [...] ويبين أن الأطفال الذين ينشؤون في أسر مستقرة ذات والدين، مقارنة بغيرهم، يتمتعون بمستوى معيشة أعلى، ويتلقون تربية أكثر فاعلية، ويعيشون تعاونا أكبر بين والديهم، وهم أقرب عاطفيا إلى كلا الوالدين، ويتعرضون لأحداث وظروف ضاغطة أقل.
double_edged: the estimated effects of parental divorce on children's well-being are modest rather than strong [...] Some children with divorced parents cope well [...] He finds that interventions that increase the share of children who grow up with both parents would improve the overall well-being of U.S. children only modestly, because children's social or emotional problems have many causes, of which family structure is but one.
notes: Full text reproduced on cyc-net.org (official: Project MUSE / Princeton-Brookings, doi:10.1353/foc.2005.0012; PubMed 16158731 bot-checked). The gist's attribution of the gap to «موارد الأب وصلته» is not the article's framing: it attributes the differences to the resources of the stable two-parent family (income, parenting, co-parenting, closeness to BOTH parents, fewer stressors); the father-specific line in the body is only «losing contact with fathers is one of the most painful outcomes of divorce». Suggest softening the gist; the article also stresses that the effects of divorce are modest.

found_text: The impact of father absence on early sexual activity and teenage pregnancy was investigated in longitudinal studies in the United States (N = 242) and New Zealand (N = 520), in which community samples of girls were followed prospectively from early in life (5 years) to approximately age 18. Greater exposure to father absence was strongly associated with elevated risk for early sexual activity and adolescent pregnancy.
location: Abstract (sentences 1-2), Child Development 74(3):801-821 (2003), doi:10.1111/1467-8624.00569 (full text also in PMC: PMC2764264)
proposed_ar: درس أثر غياب الأب في النشاط الجنسي المبكر والحمل في سن المراهقة في دراستي متابعة في الولايات المتحدة (242 بنتا) ونيوزيلندا (520 بنتا)، تتبعت فيهما عينات من البنات من سن 5 سنوات إلى نحو 18 سنة. وكان التعرض الأكبر لغياب الأب مرتبطا ارتباطا قويا بارتفاع خطر النشاط الجنسي المبكر والحمل في المراهقة.
notes: Abstract verified on the Duke Scholars record (PubMed/PMC bot-checked). The gist's «كان الأثر أشد كلما بكر غياب الأب» is from the body, not the abstract; the authors' Duke press release (https://today.duke.edu/2003/06/dodge605.html) states pregnancy rates were «seven to eight times higher among early father-absent girls» but «only two to three times higher among later father-absent girls, than among father-present girls» (early = father left before age 6). The abstract also says the risk was not (US) or only partly (NZ) explained by other disadvantages.

found_text: Children in joint physical or legal custody were better adjusted than children in sole-custody settings, but no different from those in intact families. More positive adjustment of joint-custody children held for separate comparisons of general adjustment, family relationships, self-esteem, emotional and behavioral adjustment, and divorce-specific adjustment. Joint-custody parents reported less current and past conflict than sole-custody parents, but this did not explain the better adjustment of joint-custody children.
location: Abstract (sentences 2-4), Journal of Family Psychology 16(1):91-102 (2002), doi:10.1037/0893-3200.16.1.91; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1037/0893-3200.16.1.91)
proposed_ar: كان الأطفال في الحضانة المشتركة، البدنية أو القانونية، أحسن توافقا من الأطفال في الحضانة المنفردة، ولم يختلفوا عن أطفال الأسر المتماسكة. وثبت التوافق الأفضل لأطفال الحضانة المشتركة في مقارنات منفصلة للتوافق العام، والعلاقات الأسرية، وتقدير الذات، والتوافق العاطفي والسلوكي، والتوافق الخاص بالطلاق. وأبلغ والدو الحضانة المشتركة عن نزاع حالي وسابق أقل من والدي الحضانة المنفردة، لكن ذلك لم يفسر التوافق الأفضل لأطفال الحضانة المشتركة.
double_edged: The results are consistent with the hypothesis that joint custody can be advantageous for children in some cases, possibly by facilitating ongoing positive involvement with both parents.
notes: Gist accurate. Meta-analysis of 33 studies. Caution: it pools joint PHYSICAL and joint LEGAL custody («joint physical or legal custody»), so it is not purely about equal-time arrangements, and the author hedges («in some cases»). PubMed and APA PsycNet blocked (robots); verified via OpenAlex.

found_text: In the 60 studies published in English in academic journals or in government reports, 34 studies found that JPC children had better outcomes on all of the measures of behavioral, emotional, physical, and academic well-being and relationships with parents and grandparents. [...] In sum, independent of family income or parental conflict, JPC is generally linked to better outcomes for children.
location: Abstract, Journal of Child Custody 15(1):35-54 (2018), doi:10.1080/15379418.2017.1422414; abstract reproduced on p. 1 of Linda Nielsen's written testimony to the Kansas Senate Judiciary Committee on SB 257 (30 January 2018)
proposed_ar: في الدراسات الستين المنشورة بالإنجليزية في المجلات العلمية أو التقارير الحكومية، وجدت 34 دراسة أن أطفال الإقامة المشتركة كانت نتائجهم أفضل في جميع مقاييس السلامة السلوكية والعاطفية والبدنية والدراسية وفي علاقاتهم بالوالدين والأجداد. [...] وخلاصة القول: بصرف النظر عن دخل الأسرة أو النزاع بين الوالدين، ترتبط الإقامة المشتركة عموما بنتائج أفضل للأطفال.
double_edged: In the 19 studies that included parental conflict, JPC children had better outcomes on all measures in 9 studies, equal to better outcomes in 5 studies, equal outcomes in 2 studies, and worse outcomes on one measure but equal or better outcomes on other measures in 3 studies.
notes: Gist accurate. Narrative review of 60 studies; in Nielsen's reviews JPC means at least 35% of time with each parent (not necessarily equal). Income sentence: «In the 25 studies that considered family income, JPC children had better outcomes on all measures in 18 studies, equal to better outcomes in 4 studies, equal outcomes in 1 study, and worse outcomes on one measure but equal or better outcomes on other measures in 2 studies.» Publisher (T&F) blocked; verified from the author's own testimony reproducing the abstract.

proposed_ar: كان ضعف التواصل مع الأم والأب معا أقل احتمالا بدرجة ملحوظة في الإقامة المشتركة منه في الأسر الأخرى غير المتماسكة. وكان ضعف التواصل مع الأم متساوي الشيوع في الأسر المتماسكة وأسر الإقامة المشتركة، بينما كان ضعف التواصل مع الأب أقل شيوعا في الواقع في الإقامة المشتركة منه في الأسر المتماسكة.

Publisher (UTP) and doi.org could not be fetched; the Icelandic repository record (rafhladan.is/handle/10802/25033) confirms the citation but has restricted full text.

location: Abstract (sentences 2 and 5), Journal of Divorce & Remarriage 59(5):452-468 (2018), doi:10.1080/10502556.2018.1454203; author manuscript in DigitalCommons@University of Nebraska-Lincoln
proposed_ar: ومع أن عدة مقالات مراجعة لخصت ما يصل إلى 61 دراسة ميدانية وأظهرت إجابات إيجابية جدا، فإن كثيرا من تصاميم البحث المستعملة تضعف القدرة على الجزم بأن الإقامة المشتركة نفسها، لا أثر الانتقاء، هي سبب هذا الأثر. proposed_ar: لم يكن تكرار الاتصال بالآباء غير المقيمين مرتبطا بنتائج الأطفال على العموم. أما البعدان الآخران من علاقة الأب بالطفل، وهما الشعور بالقرب والتربية الحازمة الحانية، فكانا مرتبطين إيجابا بنجاح الأطفال الدراسي، وسلبا بمشكلاتهم السلوكية الظاهرة ومشكلاتهم النفسية الداخلية.
double_edged: The frequency of contact with nonresident fathers was not related to child outcomes in general.
notes: Gist accurate (quality of fathering, not mere visiting, predicts outcomes). Double-edged for a pure «more time» argument: the meta-analysis found visitation FREQUENCY unrelated to outcomes (it concerns visiting, not shared residence). First sentence of abstract: «We employed meta-analytic methods to pool information from 63 studies dealing with nonresident fathers and children's well-being» (last word inferred from position gap). doi.org redirects to JSTOR (not fetchable by bot); verified via OpenAlex.

found_text: In sum, there is empirical evidence from different countries that suggests that JPC arrangements can have positive effects on the well-being of children and parents. However, the existing studies are conceptually, methodologically, and contextually very heterogeneous. In addition, self-selected highly educated parents with a high socio-economic status, a low conflict level, and children between the ages of 6-15 practicing JPC dominate the samples. Thus, the risks and benefits of JPC are not clear yet and are heavily debated by advocates and academics.
location: Abstract (sentences 5-8), Family Process 58(2):353-369 (2019; online 2018), doi:10.1111/famp.12372; 40 studies 2007-2018; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1111/famp.12372)
proposed_ar: وخلاصة القول: هناك أدلة ميدانية من بلدان مختلفة توحي بأن ترتيبات الإقامة المشتركة يمكن أن تكون لها آثار إيجابية في رفاه الأطفال والوالدين. غير أن الدراسات الموجودة شديدة التباين في مفاهيمها ومناهجها وسياقاتها. يضاف إلى ذلك أن العينات يغلب عليها آباء وأمهات اختاروا هذا الترتيب بأنفسهم، من ذوي التعليم العالي والمكانة الاجتماعية والاقتصادية المرتفعة وقلة النزاع، وأطفال بين 6 و15 سنة. ولذلك فإن مخاطر الإقامة المشتركة ومنافعها ليست واضحة بعد، وهي موضع جدل شديد بين المناصرين والأكاديميين.
double_edged: Thus, the risks and benefits of JPC are not clear yet and are heavily debated by advocates and academics.
notes: Gist partly accurate: the abstract says JPC «can have positive effects», but its reservations are about heterogeneity and self-selection (not specifically «high conflict» as the gist says), and it concludes that risks and benefits «are not clear yet». JPC defined here as at least 25-50% of time with each parent. PubMed and Wiley blocked; verified via OpenAlex.

found_text: While professionals agree that children of separation and divorce fare best when they have stable, healthy, and continuing contact with both parents, reaching a consensus about shared parenting policy has been elusive. [...] Still others raise concerns about the wisdom of any legal presumption, particularly in cases involving infants and toddlers, high conflict, and domestic violence. Some of these professionals take a more circumspect approach, contending that, because one size never fits all, parenting time must be determined on a case-by-case basis, preferably by the parents themselves.
location: Abstract (paragraph 1 sentence 3; paragraph 2 sentences 9-10), Family Court Review 52(2):152-174 (2014), doi:10.1111/fcre.12078; pre-publication copy at Hofstra Law Scholarly Commons. Report consensus point 10 (p. 168): "Children's best interests are furthered by parenting plans that provide for continuing and shared parenting relationships"
proposed_ar: ومع أن المختصين متفقون على أن أطفال الانفصال والطلاق يكونون أحسن حالا حين يكون لهم اتصال مستقر وصحي ومستمر بكلا الوالدين، فإن الوصول إلى إجماع على سياسة الرعاية المشتركة ظل عسيرا. [...] ويبدي آخرون قلقا من حكمة أي أصل قانوني مفترض، ولا سيما في الحالات التي تشمل الرضع والصغار، والنزاع الشديد، والعنف الأسري. ويتخذ بعض هؤلاء المختصين نهجا أكثر تحفظا، إذ يرون أنه لا يوجد مقاس واحد يناسب الجميع، ولذلك يجب تحديد وقت الرعاية لكل حالة على حدة، ويفضل أن يحدده الوالدان أنفسهما.
double_edged: Statutory presumptions prescribing specific allocations of shared parenting time are unsupportable (p. 154) [...] It is inappropriate to have a presumption that covers all situations when not enough is known (p. 168) [...] A majority of the think tank professionals supported a presumption of joint decision making (p. 167)
notes: The gist misstates the Think Tank's conclusion. The AFCC Think Tank (32 experts) agreed that children benefit from continuing and shared parenting RELATIONSHIPS and a majority supported a presumption of joint DECISION-MAKING, but it explicitly rejected statutory presumptions of specific shared-parenting TIME allocations (equal time) and said one size never fits all. For an equal-time thesis this entry is double-edged; if kept, reword to: agreement on continuing involvement of both parents, no presumption of equal time. Full report: https://www.afccnet.org/Portals/0/PDF/Final%20Think%20Tank%20Report.pdf ; PDF of article: https://scholarlycommons.law.hofstra.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1404&context=faculty_scholarship. Wiley blocked.

proposed_ar: نسأل: هل الأطفال في الرعاية المشتركة بالمناصفة أكثر احتمالا للإبلاغ عن مستويات عالية من الضغط النفسي مقارنة بالأطفال الذين يعيشون في حضانة أحد الوالدين؟ [...] وتبين النتائج أن الأطفال الذين يتقاسمون الإقامة بالتساوي بين الوالدين أقل احتمالا لأن يعانوا مستويات عالية من الضغط النفسي. ويمكن تفسير النتائج على أنها دليل على أثر إيجابي لاستمرار علاقة يومية طبيعية بالوالدين بعد تفكك الأسرة.
notes: Gist accurate; «sharing residence equally» justifies «الرعاية المشتركة بالمناصفة». Swedish ULF survey data 2001-2003 combined with registers (807 children per the Population Europe summary); models controlled for interparental conflict, parent-child relationship quality and parents' income. Publisher (T&F) blocked; verified via OpenAlex (one word, «conflict», missing from the index in the control-variables sentence).

found_text: Recent research does not support the idea that conflict—including high legal conflict—should rule out joint physical custody as the arrangement that best serves children's interests. [...] Conflict and poor coparenting are not linked to worse outcomes for children in joint physical custody than in sole physical custody. The quality of the parent–child relationship is a better predictor than conflict of children's outcomes, with the exception of the most extreme forms of conflict to which some children are exposed.
location: Abstract (sentences 5, 7-8), Psychology, Public Policy, and Law 23(2):211-231 (2017), doi:10.1037/law0000109; abstract reproduced in full on Palo Alto University's 'Translating Research into Practice' blog
proposed_ar: لا تؤيد البحوث الحديثة فكرة أن النزاع، بما فيه النزاع القضائي الشديد، ينبغي أن يستبعد الإقامة المشتركة بوصفها الترتيب الذي يخدم مصالح الأطفال على أفضل وجه. [...] والنزاع وسوء تعاون الوالدين لا يرتبطان بنتائج أسوأ للأطفال في الإقامة المشتركة منها في الحضانة المنفردة. وجودة علاقة الطفل بوالديه أقدر على التنبؤ بنتائج الأطفال من النزاع، باستثناء أشد صور النزاع التي يتعرض لها بعض الأطفال.
double_edged: with the exception of the most extreme forms of conflict to which some children are exposed.
notes: JPC here = children living at least 35% of the time with each parent. The abstract says conflict is not linked to WORSE outcomes in JPC than in sole custody; it does not say JPC children are better off under conflict, so the gist's «أحسن حالا في الغالب حتى مع نزاع» should be softened to «ليسوا أسوأ حالا». APA PsycNet blocked (robots); OpenAlex and CrossRef carry no abstract; verified from the PAU blog which reproduces the abstract under an 'Abstract' heading.

found_text: Students endorsed living arrangements that gave them equal time with their fathers, they had better outcomes when they had such arrangements and when their parents supported their time with the other parent, they experienced disagreement between mothers and fathers over living arrangements, and they gave evidence of their fathers' continuing commitment to them into their young adult years.
location: Abstract (sentence 2), Family Relations 52(4):385-396 (2003), doi:10.1111/j.1741-3729.2003.00385.x; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1111/j.1741-3729.2003.00385.x)
proposed_ar: أيد الطلاب ترتيبات الإقامة التي تعطيهم وقتا متساويا مع آبائهم، وكانت نتائجهم أفضل حين كانت لهم مثل هذه الترتيبات وحين دعم والداهم وقتهم مع الطرف الآخر، وعاشوا خلافا بين الأمهات والآباء حول ترتيبات الإقامة، وقدموا ما يدل على استمرار التزام آبائهم بهم إلى سنوات شبابهم.
notes: Gist accurate: college students (Arizona State) whose parents had divorced endorsed EQUAL time with fathers; the «wished more time with fathers» clause is from the body, not the abstract. Final abstract sentence: «These findings consistently contradict the recent, influential public policy recommendations of Judith Wallerstein.» Wiley blocked; OpenAlex reconstruction (word at position 68 confirmed as «such»).

location: Abstract (sentence 1), American Journal of Family Therapy 40(1):33-55 (2012), doi:10.1080/01926187.2011.575344; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1080/01926187.2011.575344)
proposed_ar: تعرض [المقالة] ستة عشر حجة تؤيد جعل المسؤولية الأبوية المتساوية أصلا مفترضا في نزاعات الحضانة، من منظور يركز على الطفل، وتقابل الأدلة العلاجية والميدانية المؤيدة لكل حجة بالأدلة المعارضة.
notes: The abstract is generic; the specific benefits in the gist come from the body. Kruk's own summary (Psychology Today, April 2012, which states the 16 arguments are from this article) lists among them: «Shared parenting preserves children's relationships with both parents» (#1), «Shared parenting decreases parental conflict and prevents family violence» (#3), «Shared parenting decreases parental focus on 'mathematizing time' and reduces litigation» (#8), «Shared parenting reduces the risk and incidence of parental alienation» (#11) — https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/co-parenting-after-divorce/201204/sixteen-arguments-in-support-co-parenting . Article body not accessible (T&F blocked).

found_text: In the Netherlands between 1998 and 2008, joint physical custody after divorce (when children actually have shared residences) has increased from 5% to 16%. [...] The main conclusion is that, on average, the effects of joint physical custody for children, mothers, and especially for fathers, are slightly positive.
location: Abstract (sentences 2 and 4), Journal of Divorce & Remarriage 51(1):65-82 (2010; online December 2009), doi:10.1080/10502550903423362; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1080/10502550903423362)
proposed_ar: في هولندا بين 1998 و2008 ارتفعت نسبة الإقامة المشتركة بعد الطلاق (حين يقيم الأطفال فعلا في بيتي الوالدين) من 5% إلى 16%. [...] والخلاصة الرئيسية أن آثار الإقامة المشتركة في الأطفال والأمهات، وفي الآباء خاصة، إيجابية طفيفة في المتوسط.
notes: Gist acceptable but the abstract's wording is «slightly positive» on average — convey «إيجابية طفيفة». Comparison groups: mother-custody with low vs high father contact, co-parenting (JPC) families, father families. CrossRef dates the article 2009 (print volume 51(1) is 2010). The Utrecht University record found by search is the 2008 conference version without abstract. Publisher (T&F) blocked; verified via OpenAlex.

proposed_ar: لا توجد نظرية متماسكة ولا بحث يؤكد الظنون القائلة بأن رعاية الأب لصغاره ليلا تحمل مخاطر أكبر من رعايتهم نهارا، أو أن المبيت ممنوع إذا عارضته الأم. والنظرية والبحث والاعتبارات العملية تؤيد منافع المبيت.

found_text: Children in JPC report better well-being and mental health than children who live mostly or only with 1 parent. No Swedish studies have found children's health to be worse in JPC than in sole parental care from child age of 3 years and beyond.
location: Abstract (sentences 4-5), Journal of Divorce & Remarriage 59(5):349-358 (2018), doi:10.1080/10502556.2018.1454198; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1080/10502556.2018.1454198)
proposed_ar: يبلغ الأطفال في الرعاية المشتركة بالمناصفة عن رفاه وصحة نفسية أفضل من الأطفال الذين يعيشون في الغالب أو كليا مع أحد الوالدين. ولم تجد أي دراسة سويدية أن صحة الأطفال في الرعاية المشتركة بالمناصفة أسوأ منها في رعاية أحد الوالدين وحده من سن 3 سنوات فما فوق.
double_edged: The existing literature cannot, however, inform us about the mechanisms behind the findings. The risks of selection effects into living arrangements are plausible.
notes: Gist accurate. JPC defined in the abstract as «children living alternatively and about equally with both parents», so «الرعاية المشتركة بالمناصفة» fits. Evidence is stated for ages 3 and above only. Publisher (T&F) blocked; verified via OpenAlex.

found_text: Living in a joint physical custody arrangement was positively related to children's mental health, whereas high levels of interparental conflict were negatively related to children's mental health. However, when levels of interparental conflict were high children in joint physical custody arrangements displayed levels of mental health problems that were quite similar to those of children in sole physical custody arrangements.
location: Abstract, 'Results' paragraph, Journal of Family Research 33(3):613-636 (2021), doi:10.20377/jfr-621; FAMOD study 2019, 1,087 post-separation families
proposed_ar: كان العيش في ترتيب الإقامة المشتركة مرتبطا إيجابا بالصحة النفسية للأطفال، بينما كان ارتفاع النزاع بين الوالدين مرتبطا سلبا بصحتهم النفسية. غير أنه عند ارتفاع النزاع بين الوالدين أظهر أطفال الإقامة المشتركة مستويات من المشكلات النفسية قريبة جدا من مستويات أطفال الحضانة المنفردة.
double_edged: The findings emphasize that joint physical custody is not a "one-size-fits-all model" that is suitable for all post-separation families, and that it is only beneficial for children's mental health when interparental conflict is low.
notes: Open access; verified on the journal site (PDF: https://ubp.uni-bamberg.de/jfr/index.php/jfr/article/view/621/602). The gist («لم يكن أسوأ حالا ... حتى مع وجود نزاع») is literally true (never worse than sole custody), but the author's own conclusion is cautionary: JPC is «only beneficial ... when interparental conflict is low». Decide whether to keep.

found_text: This article summarizes panel discussions that took place at an international conference on shared parenting (SP) held in May 2017. The panelists were internationally recognized experts on the legal and psychological implications of custody arrangements and parenting plans. Seven broad themes dominated the discussions: whether or not there was persuasive evidence that SP provides real benefits to children whose parents separate; what specific factors make SP beneficial; what symbolic value SP might have; whether there should be a legal presumption in favor of SP, and if so, what factors should make for exceptions; [...]
location: Abstract, Journal of Divorce & Remarriage 59(5):372-387 (2018), doi:10.1080/10502556.2018.1454195; text obtained from the OpenAlex record (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1080/10502556.2018.1454195)
proposed_ar: تلخص هذه المقالة مناقشات الجلسات التي جرت في مؤتمر دولي عن الرعاية المشتركة عقد في مايو 2017. وكان المشاركون خبراء معترفا بهم دوليا في الآثار القانونية والنفسية لترتيبات الحضانة وخطط الرعاية. وهيمنت على المناقشات سبعة موضوعات واسعة: هل هناك دليل مقنع على أن الرعاية المشتركة تحقق منافع حقيقية للأطفال الذين ينفصل والداهم؛ وما العوامل التي تجعلها نافعة؛ وما قيمتها الرمزية؛ وهل ينبغي أن يكون هناك أصل قانوني مفترض لصالحها، وإن كان فما العوامل التي تستوجب الاستثناء؛ [...]
notes: The abstract only lists the seven themes; the gist's «أكثرهم يرون ... نافعة ... مع استثناء حالات العنف» comes from the body, which was not accessible (T&F blocked). The Child & Family Blog summary of the article (October 2018, https://childandfamilyblog.com/shared-parenting-after-divorce/) states in its own words: «Most, but not all, of the panellists believed that the evidence supports making shared parenting a legal presumption» and that «the only form the experts agreed should preclude shared parenting is coercive, controlling violence» — consistent with the gist but not the article's wording. Remaining themes: high conflict / failure to agree / parental alienation as possible bars, and relocation. Lamb is at Cambridge (UK), Braver at Arizona State.

Adolescents from single father families reported an alarmingly high amount of antisocial behavior and substance use

proposed_ar: كان المراهقون من أسر الأم الوحيدة وأسر زوج الأم معرضين لخطر متزايد باعتدال لإظهار مشكلات توافق متنوعة مقارنة بالمراهقين من أسر الوالدين غير المطلقين [...] بينما لم يكن نظراؤهم من أسر الإقامة المشتركة معرضين لخطر أعلى من أقرانهم من الأسر غير المطلقة إلا في مجال التحصيل الدراسي. وأبلغ المراهقون من أسر الأب الوحيد عن قدر مقلق جدا من السلوك المعادي للمجتمع وتعاطي المواد المخدرة.
double_edged: their counterparts from families with joint physical custody were at no higher risk of displaying adjustment problems than their peers from non-divorced families except in the area of school achievement
notes: Verified on the Informa Healthcare mirror of the publisher page (tandfonline blocked). The gist's direct comparison («أحسن توافقا من ... الأم وحدها أو ... الأب وحده») is an inference: the abstract compares each structure with non-divorced families (JPC = no higher risk except school achievement; single-mother/stepfather = moderately increased risk; single-father = alarmingly high antisocial behavior and substance use). The «[...]» marks a conjunction not captured verbatim. Note the school-achievement exception.
